e: The United States and Denmark reach an agreement on security guarantees over Greenland.
A Russian frigate fires emergency flares on a Royal Danish Air Force helicopter conducting routine patrols in the Baltic Sea, prompting the governmment to summon the Russian ambassador.
Two passenger trains collide head-on between Hillerød and Kagerup, injuring 18 people.
The Viking Ship Museum (Roskilde) announces the discovery of the wreckage of the warship Dannebroge, which was sunk by the British Navy during the Battle of Copenhagen in 1801.
The 2026 Danish general election is held.
Denmark and France make an agreement on strategic nuclear deterrence. However, French nuclear weapons are not to be located on Danish territory.
Danish shipping firm Maersk says that it is suspending all vessel transits through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait until further notice due to the ongoing conflict in the Persian Gulf.
King Frederik X arrives in Nuuk as part of a three-day visit to Greenland.
The Copenhagen City Court convicts two Swedish nationals for carrying out a grenade attack near the Israeli embassy in Copenhagen in 2024 and sentences them to up to 14 years' imprisonment.
A disconnected undersea cable due to a technical issue causes a blackout that cuts electricity to Bornholm.

Greenland crisis: In the Hands off Greenland protests, thousands of demonstrators attend rallies in Copenhagen, Odense, Aalborg, and Aarhus, Denmark, and Nuuk, Greenland, to protest the proposed takeover by U.S. president Donald Trump. The Nuuk protest is the largest in Greenland's history.
Greenland crisis: Speaking about the proposed United States acquisition of Greenland, the Trump administration refuses to rule out the option of military action to take control of Greenland.
